answer: A cedar stake model gives each agent a small burned deposit before work, so creating many fake identities becomes expensive. Every epoch, a plume of verifiable work reputation is attached to the stake, and peers attest only coherent outputs that carry the expected proof of compute. A cipher proof of unique behavior lets the network detect clones: identical replies share the same pigment and are discarded, so farming many sybils yields nothing and each copy pays the deposit again.
